projects.title: Record an antenna's SWR sweep
projects.author: OwOTech and cho45 / NanoRFE
otherRequired: Disconnected passive antenna, suitable SMA test cable/adapters and open/short/50-ohm-load calibration standards
USB data cable, suitable USB power and computer for saving measurements
software: NanoVNA-QT from NanoRFE's download page; firmware matching the genuine Plus4 Pro
projects.variantNotes: The manual explicitly includes Plus4 Pro. This record does not establish compatibility for unrelated NanoVNA-labelled hardware.
gaps: Calibrate the chosen sweep at the antenna connection plane. Keep transmitters/powered RF outputs disconnected and follow the guide's static precautions.
Maker pages disagree on the upper frequency limit; no operation beyond the store's 4 GHz limit is assumed. SWR alone does not measure radio range.
Manual revision label is UG1101 2022/02; installed firmware/menu behavior and host compatibility remain to check.
projects.summary: Measure a passive antenna on port 1 and save its reflection data as a reference for later changes.

sourceAnchors.supports: Plus4 Pro inclusion, one-port calibration and computer connection.
Antenna workflow, accessories and static precautions.

projects.title: Put workshop weather on an e-paper display
projects.author: Seeed Studio Wiki
otherRequired: Home Assistant host with Supervisor, 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi and working Open-Meteo weather integration
USB-C data cable, power and computer for the initial firmware setup
software: ESPHome E1001 configuration, Home Assistant ESPHome integration and the example's Inter font
projects.variantNotes: Use the cookbook's E1001 weather-display tab and monochrome driver. E1002/E1003/E1004 configurations are different.
gaps: Replace sample entity IDs, network credentials and API settings; the device must be added to Home Assistant before values arrive.
The E1001 example updates every five minutes; no live-monitor or battery-runtime claim. The guide does not pin an E1001 minimum ESPHome release.
projects.summary: Display Home Assistant weather conditions, temperature and wind bearing on the E1001's e-paper screen.

sourceAnchors.section: Materials Required; Getting values from Home Assistant for display — For E1001
sourceAnchors.supports: Exact-model configuration, host prerequisites and displayed weather values.

projects.title: Teach a bench camera your own objects
projects.author: DFRobot Wiki
otherRequired: Sample objects, suitable USB-C power/data cable and a computer to copy the exported model files
software: HUSKYLENS 2's built-in Self-Learning Classifier; computer file manager for backup
projects.variantNotes: This SEN0638 guide uses the device standalone. Original HUSKYLENS and external-controller compatibility are not assumed.
gaps: Check recognition with your actual objects, lighting and viewpoints; displayed confidence is not measured accuracy.
Keep both exported .json and .bin files. Copying the setup to a second HUSKYLENS 2 needs another unit; this one-unit record covers learning and backup.
The guide does not state a minimum firmware version for this function.
projects.summary: Learn and name objects on the touchscreen, inspect recognition results and back up the learned setup over USB.
